trust_decision.summary: Whether a client may dispatch @event_handler calls is decided at WebSocket mount time in LiveViewConsumer.handle_mount (check_view_auth, then close-the-socket on denial); the event path itself trusts only 'self.view_instance is set' and never re-runs the auth check.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names a 'login_required / on_mount LiveView mount redirect' that does not close the socket; an engineer reading that looks straight at the 'if redirect_url:' branch of handle_mount, which sends {'type':'navigate'} and returns without self.close().

fix_sites.entry_point: WebSocket frame {"type":"mount"} (receive dispatch, websocket.py:1625) and {"type":"live_redirect_mount"} (websocket.py:1633 -> handle_live_redirect_mount at websocket.py:4290, which delegates to handle_mount)
same mount entries, redirect returned by an on_mount hook (run_on_mount_hooks, websocket.py:2002)

fix_sites.where: python/djust/websocket.py:2524-2537 (the fix adds the _mounting_in_batch suppression flag here, with its two restore points at fix.diff:410-416 and fix.diff:423-432)
fix_sites.module_kind: batch mount helper inside the consumer

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The SSE transport is presented as a degraded fallback (no presence, no actors, one-way stream) whose event endpoint is labelled legacy ('POST /djust/sse/<session_id>/event/' at docs/sse-transport.md:17), and the project documents auth as mount-time-only by design (docs/guides/authentication.md:197-201), so a solver can argue both the SSE mount and the missing per-event re-check are outside the advisory's WebSocket transport.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A login-redirecting view mounted inside a multiplexed mount_batch on a shared socket must NOT close that socket: sibling public views keep serving events and the redirect is reported in the batch's navigate[] array; an unconditional close in the redirect branch kills the whole batch, so the fix threads a _mounting_in_batch flag through _mount_one to suppress only the close.

O6_input_shapes: auth redirect: check_view_auth returns LOGIN_URL for anonymous (login_required), permission-less anonymous, or custom check_permissions() returning False
hook redirect: run_on_mount_hooks returns a redirect target
single mount frame on its own socket (close is allowed)
multiplexed mount_batch entry on a shared socket (close must be suppressed, the unmounted view must still be cleared)
live_redirect_mount, which re-enters handle_mount on an already-open socket

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SSE legacy event path: GET /djust/sse/<id>/?view=<login_required view> mounts through _sse_mount_view, pushes navigate and returns with session.view_instance still set; POST /djust/sse/<id>/event/ then dispatches to @event_handler unauthenticated because the stream is never shut down and the session stays registered
O8_uncovered_routes.where: python/djust/sse.py:242-244 (mount redirect), with the sink at python/djust/sse.py:352-355 and python/djust/sse.py:785-810
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: SSE is a fallback transport and /event/ is documented as the legacy endpoint (docs/sse-transport.md:10-17); the advisory and its remediation talk only about WebSocket close codes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another module in the same package, a separate hand-written mount implementation that the published diff never touches

O8_uncovered_routes.route: No auth re-check on the live event path: a socket that mounted legitimately keeps dispatching @event_handler calls after the user logs out or loses the permission - the same sink, reached without any mount redirect
O8_uncovered_routes.where: python/djust/websocket.py:2722-2724 (handle_event gates only on self.view_instance; no check_view_auth call in its body)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: docs/guides/authentication.md:195-201 states mount-time-only auth as a conscious, documented trade-off shared with Phoenix/Livewire, so a solver can call a per-event re-check a new feature rather than part of this fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: about 700 lines below the landing point in the same file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second mount implementation (long-poll / SSE / fallback transport) that pushes navigate but never clears session.view_instance and never shuts the transport down
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _sse_mount_view is a hand-copied mirror of handle_mount whose docstring claims the same security model (python/djust/sse.py:159-166), so a maintainer re-implementing the branch would plausibly copy the 'send navigate, return' shape and forget the close.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a transport built on the shared ViewRuntime that clears runtime.view_instance on an auth block but never terminates its own transport, leaving the session lingering
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: runtime.py is explicitly the transport-agnostic seam for new transports (ADR-016) and each transport owns its own Transport object, so a new transport can easily omit a shutdown call.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third denial branch (object-permission, post-mount) that sends an error and closes but never clears view_instance - or the reverse, a copied branch that clears but forgets to close
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same function already contains three denial branches written at different times; copy-paste of one branch into a new lifecycle stage is exactly the parallel-path drift the fix comments warn about (#1646).

O9_family: improper authorization / missing authentication check on a live event-dispatch channel (CWE-285, CWE-306)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the early return in handle_mount's redirect branch with an unconditional await self.close(code=4403), which fixes the single-mount case but kills multiplexed mount_batch siblings and drops the navigate frame the batch response needs.
